One of the limitations with the developed application is that all the content was 
produced by a human, which not only takes time but the content maybe fallible, 
and not appeal to all students learning styles. Utilisation of machine learning 
systems to create new student specific content, could also pose as a lucrative 
area of research given the recent generative artificial intelligent revolution. A 
system of this nature could gradually over time adapt lessons to better motivate 
and engage students, to improve their educational outcomes. Looking at the 
forefront of AI technologies utilisation of pretrained models such as Open AIs 
Sora, could generate short form video content for individual students (Open AI, 
n.d.). This would build off the findings from Chapter 5 regarding improved 
academic performance and would stand as an application that could possibly 
revolutionise the industry.  
Expanding the application’s user base poses as another avenue for future 
research. Analysing the application’s effectiveness on a large scale, allows for 
tests across multiple demographics and geographical regions. Prototype tests 
varying educational settings, including varying countries and cultures, would 
provide valuable insights into the generalisability of a short-form content 
delivery system.  
Finally, a longitudinal study as highlighted in 5.8, would be key to expand upon 
and evaluate the effects of gamified short-form content on students. Although 
the results found here are promising, they only assess the students within a ten-
minute time window. Revealing the impact of these methodologies over multiple 
months or even years, is crucial for understanding the effects on deep learning 
and content mastery. These studies would help the understanding of how 
students retain this knowledge and how their performance changes over time.
